fatal_errors: The hypothesis conflates beneficial composition-induced lattice distortion with thermally induced lattice disorder; these can have opposite effects on strength and wear.
Its predicted direction conflicts with the target behavior: rapid disorder above about 900 K reduces hardness and wear resistance rather than improving them.
The proposed intervention does not operationally define how disorder will be varied while holding composition, phases, coating geometry, substrate, temperature, and contact conditions constant.
The baseline is a different alloy class rather than the same FeNiCrCoCu coating at 300 K, preventing attribution to the proposed mediator.
No quantitative temperature or disorder range is specified, and the critical approximately 900 K transition is omitted.
explanation: The response recognizes that atomic structure can mediate HEA coating wear through mechanical properties, so it is relevant and broadly plausible. However, it does not reconstruct the temperature-controlled nanoindentation/friction study, its FeNiCrCoCu/Cu model, or the observed nonmonotonic modulus and sharp high-temperature softening. The cited literature generally supports HEA wear resistance and, in selected systems, strengthening from compositional lattice distortion or secondary phases; it does not establish a universal monotonic benefit from increasing atomic disorder. Listing all evidence without distinguishing direct support, indirect background, and potentially conflicting regimes weakens evidence discipline. The proposed correlation study is also poorly discriminating because composition and processing changes would alter phases, hardness, residual stress, and chemistry alongside disorder. A valid test would vary temperature from 300 to 1200 K on an otherwise identical coating and jointly measure HCP fraction, dislocation line length, hardness/modulus, tangential force, and friction coefficient, with falsification if disorder rises without the predicted high-temperature mechanical and tribological transition.
